svg.text: One bounded follow-up: same adjacent-channel setup, fixed spacing at the first settle point, sweep loop gain only.
At the first settle-point spacing, gain retuning mostly rescales the same adjacent-pull gap

text.tspan: This pass keeps spacing fixed at 1.24 R_s, adjacent power fixed at 0 dB, and sweeps only loop gain. The question is whether retuning can make the half-sine lane stop being the worse loop, or whether spacing geometry
is still doing most of the work.

svg.text: Lower gain helps both loops, but not equally

text.tspan: At gain 0.002, proxy tail pull is 0.0003 R_s and half-sine is 0.0046 R_s.
That is already much calmer than the 0.020 baseline, but half-sine is still
about 15.2x worse.

svg.text: The original 0.020 baseline was not a fluke

text.tspan: At gain 0.020, proxy stays at 0.0028 R_s with 100% of the tail inside ±0.05
R_s, while half-sine is 0.0447 R_s. The residual ranking never flips
anywhere in the tested gain set.

svg.text: By about 0.022, half-sine starts losing the settle band

text.tspan: At gain 0.022, the half-sine lane falls to 62% of tail blocks inside ±0.05
R_s, while the proxy lane is still at 100%.

svg.text: Mean tail residual CFO versus loop gain

text.tspan: Reducing gain calms both loops, but the half-sine line stays above the proxy line everywhere. This
means the spacing penalty did not turn into a one-parameter tuning problem.
The proxy lane keeps every tested gain inside the settle band. The half-sine lane is fine while gain
stays modest, then starts dropping tail blocks once the loop is driven harder.

svg.text: Half-sine / proxy residual ratio stays stubbornly high

text.tspan: This is the key readout. If retuning were really fixing the spacing problem, the residual ratio would bend down toward 1 as gain moved. Instead it sits around 15-16x on the default seeds, which says the detector
geometry is still the main story.
Making the loop gentler reduces adjacent pull, but it does not
make the half-sine lane competitive.
The original spacing-boundary baseline already captured the same
ordering that the full gain sweep keeps repeating.
Stop treating this as a tuning-only question. If the queue returns
here, it should be for a fresh geometry change or packaging, not
more same-shape gain nudging.
